title: Code Factory: Proof-by-Sabotage Software Factory
description:
Code Factory is a proof-first, open-source software factory for turning specifications, behavior checks, design contracts, policy verification, and release receipts into auditable delivery. Version 0.24 adds Unified Graph Ops: a deterministic, read-only visual overlay over existing Product Graph, slice, mission, approval, completion, proof, gate-plan, trace, receipt, and artifact facts. It emits one fact-derived next action and never executes validation, approves work, or gains release authority. Version 0.23.1 patches two high-severity transitive vulnerabilities in the VS Code build toolchain and enforces a high-severity npm audit gate in pull-request and release workflows. Version 0.23 adds content-addressed proof keys; fail-closed RUN, REUSE, SKIP, and BLOCK routing; exact input, output, toolchain, and environment verification; isolated mutation challenges; compact proof plans; and automatic paired savings receipts for verified reuse. July history contained 1101.3 measured duplicate IntelliJ runner-minutes; that value is an opportunity baseline, not prospective savings. Durable Product Missions, exact paired savings, secret-free multi-provider BYOK policies, the supervised hosted tenant control plane, authenticated pull-request assurance, signed Capability Packs, seven starter targets, and editor integrations remain included. Public documentation assets include exact Studio captures, Mermaid diagrams, and a nine-stage conceptual visual walkthrough; the illustrations are not UI screenshots or measured outcome evidence.

Evidence boundary: Graph Ops is bounded to readable local artifacts and does not claim time, token, cost, productivity, or conversion savings. The remediated packages are development-only VS Code packaging dependencies and were not bundled into the dependency-free VSIX. Proof reuse is limited to read-only validation and never grants publish, deploy, sign, approval, credential, connector, or external-message authority. Savings receipts perform arithmetic over exact observations and do not generalize beyond the recorded pairs. The hosted reference is deployable and supervised but does not claim managed HA, automatic disaster recovery, SCIM, SAML enrollment, managed KMS, SOC 2, or an SLA. A passing receipt proves the declared checks and supplied environment, not arbitrary production security.
